I am looking to fill a research post on an international project on Bayesian statistics „grammo – a grammar of models“. 
We want to let users build complex models out of larger components as if building a lego set. 
Then we find ways to automatically transform them into more efficient or otherwise better-behaved versions.

* [Applied statistics.]{.highlight1} Help us build a tool for better modelling of real-world medical and psychological data. We know how to do statistical research that affects statistical practice.
* [International connection.]{.highlight1} A project with the team of [Paul Bürkner](https://paulbuerkner.com/) (TU Dortmund, author of the [brms](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/) package), close engagement with the Stan probabilistic programming language community.
* [Would you rather code or math?]{.highlight1} The project has a primarily technical, programming part as well as primarily mathematical part. The exact mixing of these ingredients can be tuned to match your preferences.

[We offer:]{.highlight1}

* do your master's thesis or get a PhD with us
* friendly workplace
* work with experienced statisticians
* flexibility and balance with your life outside of work


I am not categorically opposed to AI, but I value human understanding and want to build reliable, legible and maintainable tools.


If interested, please write to: 

[martin.modrak@lfmotol.cuni.cz](mailto:martin.modrak@lfmotol.cuni.cz)

I'll be happy to answer your questions.

Looking forward for your messages,
Martin Modrák, Ph.D.
